articles.title: Phillies scrape into MLB playoffs after week of ‘living hell in slow motion’
articles.summary: Phillies were at risk of blowing comfortable wildcard lead. Victory over Rays deprives Diamondbacks of comeback. Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered, and Zack Wheeler delivered like a Game 7 ace to bring the Philadelphia Phillies back from the brink of collapse and send them into the playoffs.
body: The Phillies could have clinched a playoff berth as early as Wednesday before they lost four straight games and nearly coughed up their wildcard lead to Arizona. But the Phillies win on Sunday, meant they snatched the final wildcard place in the National League.
The Phillies will play Game 1 in a best-of-three wildcard series on Tuesday in Atlanta against their NL East rivals, the Braves.
“It was kind of a living hell in slow motion,” Phillies managing partner and CEO John Middleton said of Philadelphia’s nervy last week.

Elsewhere, the Texas Rangers were eliminated from postseason contention on the final day of the regular season with their 6-4 loss to the Minnesota Twins, who got a home run and three RBIs from Josh Bell to back Dean Kremer’s seven innings of one-run pitching. Texas (80-82) needed a win and a Houston loss to the Athletics. Houston, who held the division tiebreaker, were leading 8-0 in the eighth inning when the Rangers game ended.
points: Phillies were at risk of blowing comfortable wildcard lead.
Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered, and Zack Wheeler delivered like a Game 7 ace to bring the Philadelphia Phillies back from the brink of collapse and send them into the playoffs.
The Phillies will play Game 1 in a best-of-three wildcard series on Tuesday in Atlanta against their NL East rivals, the Braves.

articles.title: Snedeker says Trump ‘gets all the credit’ after US complete huge Presidents Cup comeback
articles.summary: Americans dominate final day singles contests. US president gives speech before final day. The United States made a stunning rally to capture an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title on Sunday, completing a 17-13 victory over the Internationals with Donald Trump in attendance.
body: Jacob Bridgeman secured the clinching point at Medinah by sinking a four-foot par putt at the 18th hole to defeat Australian Min Woo Lee 1-up.

The Americans improved to 14-1-1 in the biennial rivalry after trailing 10.5-7.5 entering Sunday’s 12 concluding singles matches. The Internationals were poised to end a 28-year win drought but fell short once again.
The Americans, boasting eight of the world’s 11 top-ranked golfers, won on the same suburban Chicago layout where Europe took the 2012 Ryder Cup with the famed Miracle at Medinah fightback.

“These guys never lost faith,” US captain Brandt Snedeker said. “I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah’s got a history of funny things happening, and sure enough, they went out there and played their asses off. I’m so damn proud of those guys.”

articles.title: Republic of Ireland 'raised awareness worldwide' in Israel game
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson says his players "raised awareness worldwide" after they chose not to engage in pre-match formalities with Israel.
body: The Republic of Ireland and Israel players did not shake hands and the Irish squad bowed their heads when Israel's anthem was played before their 3-0 Uefa Nations League win in Hungary.
There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon, who did not shake hands.
The fixtures, being played at neutral venues, have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

The Republic of Ireland players have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

articles.title: Nations League: Greece stun Klopp’s Germany, Netherlands sink Serbia but Gakpo hurt
articles.summary: Jürgen Klopp ‘unbothered’ despite 1-0 home defeat. Gakpo goes off in 2-1 win, Portugal edge past Norway. Greece stunned Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout.
body: Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany. Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday.

The hosts were in control for most of the game and had close to 80% possession in the first half alone. Germany were ultimately punished ⁠for sloppy defending, especially in the second half, which gave the visitors space to attack.

Felix Nmecha fired wide in the 54th minute, moments after the Greece keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis ‌had palmed a Joshua Kimmich free-kick over the bar. The Greeks then almost scored in the 66th after Kimmich lost possession in his own half, but the substitute Fotis Ioannidis fired just wide of the post.

They did better eight minutes later, with Kourbelis’s deflected low drive earning their second victory in a row after their last-gasp 2-1 win over Serbia on Thursday. Greece will now host the Dutch on Thursday, while Germany are at home to Serbia.
points: Gakpo goes off in 2-1 win, Portugal edge past Norway.
Greece stunned Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout.
Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany.

articles.title: McTominay’s role a poser for Pocognoli as Scotland offer positives in Slovenia
articles.summary: New coach still learning about his squad as they prepare to face Switzerland with the Napoli midfielder expected to return in November. An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one.
body: The scoreless draw in Slovenia on Saturday raised the question of where McTominay will fit in when he returns. “He can play in many positions,” Pocognoli said. “He is a top player so he can read the game. We will see.”

Indeed we will. The answer is not immediately obvious. Pocognoli deployed Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson as central midfielders in Ljubljana with John McGinn placed ahead of them to support a two-man strike force. Gilmour was heavily influential during Scotland’s impressive second half. Ferguson’s combative and defensive skills are valuable. McGinn, like McTominay, is a mainstay of the team. It is therefore legitimate to ask how Pocognoli handles McTominay, who is expected to return to the Scotland scene in November.

“For now we just need to put the structure in place,” Pocognoli said. “I hope Scott watched the game and thought ‘OK, I see myself in that shape in the second half’, and that with good discipline he can enjoy it. I hope he can look and think: ‘Yeah, I want to play.’
“Andy Robertson was really positive after the game and said that he really enjoyed it. It is really good to hear that from top players.”
points: New coach still learning about his squad as they prepare to face Switzerland with the Napoli midfielder expected to return in November.
An elongated international window does not prevent Sébastien Pocognoli from glancing towards the next one.
The scoreless draw in Slovenia on Saturday raised the question of where McTominay will fit in when he returns.
“He can play in many positions,” Pocognoli said.

articles.title: Josh Allen injury scare is major concern for Buffalo Bills after Week 3
articles.summary: One of the NFL’s Super Bowl favorites to come out of the AFC this season is unquestionably the Buffalo Bills. They have started the season red hot at 3-0, winning high-scoring games in each of their first three weeks. The key to their success? Quarterback Josh Allen.
body: However, Allen suffered an injury scare in Week 3 that has many Bills fans and analysts concerned about the star quarterback. In the fourth quarter, Allen took a shot to his left knee. Although he didn’t leave the game, cameras captured him in clear discomfort.

It remains unclear how serious the injury could be, but one user on X offered his opinion. The account known as “Thigh Doctor,” who is also a Bills fan, provided footage of Allen during and after the game.

Thigh Doctor outlined his concerns in an X post: “Took helmet to knee at 9:46 in 4th. Grimaced. Did have one more designed run next drive. Limping postgame, leaning onto right leg, painful back-step in locker room. Contusion most likely vs MCL/meniscus.”

The good news is that the initial belief points toward a contusion rather than a tear. Notably, Allen’s leg was not fully planted on the ground at the time of impact. His foot also wasn’t firmly dug into the turf, which could have resulted in a much more serious injury.
points: One of the NFL’s Super Bowl favorites to come out of the AFC this season is unquestionably the Buffalo Bills.

However, Allen suffered an injury scare in Week 3 that has many Bills fans and analysts concerned about the star quarterback.

articles.title: Advantage in the WNBA playoffs goes to the team with A’ja Wilson, as usual
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — It is a wonderful time to be known as A’ja Wilson’s boyfriend, unless the plan is to exit a basketball arena quickly. First came the woman in the brown athleisure ensemble. She wanted a selfie with him. Then came the guy in the teal T-shirt. He requested a picture, too.
body: But Bam Adebayo, Miami Heat forward, obliged almost everyone on Sunday before he disappeared into a tunnel at Michelob Ultra Arena. Possibly because he was only star-adjacent and it was nice to get some attention in this town for once, and possibly because he understood the moment authored by the most beloved basketballer in the building deserved the memorials. It’s not every day that 10,000-plus sets of eyes watch one player unravel an entire team from start to finish. It only seems like it happens that often.

How maddening, to be the team that doesn’t have A’ja Wilson and getting scheduled to play the team that does. This is not a condition unique to the Indiana Fever, though they felt it acutely in Game 1 of a first-round playoff series here, when Wilson put her foot down and tilted the earth and the visitors slid all the way to a 102-85 defeat. This is how things have gone in the WNBA for a while. A terrifying normal, in which a world-wrecker is totally unimpressed with herself.
“I don’t think I had an out-of-body experience,” Wilson said flatly late Sunday afternoon, leaning back with a microphone in hand. “We just showed up to work.”

First came the woman in the brown athleisure ensemble.

articles.title: Why Tom Brady called Justin Herbert interception a ‘meatball sub’
articles.summary: Keeping up with the youths is no easy task. The meaning of words can change without any of the olds being aware of the switch, leaving those out of the know in troubled waters. Thankfully, for those of us a step or two behind in football’s latest trends, we have Tom Brady to keep us up to date.
body: In the booth for Fox alongside Kevin Burkhardt to call Sunday’s game between the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, Brady sounded disappointed in Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert after he threw an ugly pick over the middle.

“Herbert trying to throw down the middle of the field to Valdes-Scantling, but there’s a safety in the middle of the field. That’s Gardner-Johnson,” Brady said over the replay. “Poor awareness. Poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub.”

The term “meatball” has been in the sports world for some time — in baseball it refers to a pitch thrown right down the middle for an eager hitter to hit out of the park — but the meatball sub phenomenon in football is not as well established.

At the start of the season, several social media posts began referring to interceptions as “meatball subs,” or other various sandwiches. Some early posts seem to indicate the meme references the idea that throwing such interceptions might lead to taking a job as a sandwich artist, but now it’s simply used to refer to a real bad pick. Like so many similar language quirks, context dissolves pretty quickly.

body: Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon said "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the side booked their spot for the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

articles.title: Sunday Night Football Is The Only Way To End The Day
articles.summary: The Steelers game is officially over, and honestly, my interest in the afternoon window is hitting a wall. There is nothing quite like that post-game slump when your team has already finished their work and you’re stuck watching random matchups.
body: While the Pittsburgh fans are already checking the scores, the real action is just heating up in the late afternoon. According to Behind the Steel Curtain, the Arizona Cardinals are set to visit the San Francisco 49ers at 4:05 p.m. EST. That isn’t the only game worth your time during that window. The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers also kick off at 4:05 p.m. EST. If you want some real intensity, keep an eye on the Baltimore Ravens playing the Dallas Cowboys at 4:25 p.m. EST in Rio de Janiero. It is a solid lineup for anyone still looking for some football.

The real reason to keep the TV on is the primetime slot. Sunday Night Football is where the stars show up when the sun goes down. The Los Angeles Rams are scheduled to take on the Denver Broncos at 8:20 p.m. EST. This is the game that actually keeps the group chat alive long after the early games end. It is the perfect way to wrap up a long day of watching the league.

articles.title: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.
body: Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval.
"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

articles.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
articles.summary: Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.
body: India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.
In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."
Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

articles.title: Ravens' Tyler Loop Hits Ronaldo's ‘Siu’ After Walk-Off FG To Beat Cowboys In Brazil
articles.summary: One of soccer's most iconic celebrations showed up at the Maracanã on Sunday, courtesy of an NFL kicker. Baltimore Ravens kicker Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal as time expired Sunday to beat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31, then celebrated with Cristiano Ronaldo's "Siu" as the crowd at Maracanã…
body: The "Siu" is Ronaldo's trademark goal celebration, in which he jumps, spins in the air and lands with his feet wide and his arms at his sides while shouting "Siuuu," a stretched-out version of the Spanish word for "yes."

Loop said teammate Ryan Eckley had suggested a soccer-style knee slide after a big kick. He went with the "Siu" instead. With about three minutes left, Loop said, teammate Nick Moore told him, "We're gonna do something epic to win this game."
"Our number was called, and Nick (Moore) and Ryan and the guys up front, they all did their job, so I can do mine," Loop said. "I'm so proud of this team."

Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey made a 23-yard field goal to tie the game at 31 with seven seconds left. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson then completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and called a timeout with one second remaining, which set up Loop's kick.
